# Get-SystemDiagnostics

Collects a health snapshot of the local Windows computer and exports it as an HTML report.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Changes the system** | No, read-only |
| **Supports `-WhatIf` / `-Confirm`** | Not needed (read-only) |
| **Admin rights** | No |
| **PowerShell** | Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ |
| **Source** | [scripts/Get-SystemDiagnostics.ps1](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/scripts/Get-SystemDiagnostics.ps1) &middot; [tests](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/tests/Get-SystemDiagnostics.Tests.ps1) |

## Description

Gathers the information an L1 technician usually needs at the start of a ticket: operating system and build, uptime, CPU, memory usage, fixed disks with free space, and network adapters (IP, gateway, DNS, DHCP).

Simple health rules flag common problems (high uptime, low disk space, high memory usage, APIPA address) so the technician knows where to look.

The report is a single self-contained HTML file that can be attached to a ticket. The script only reads information; it changes nothing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-OutputPath` | String | `(Get-Location).Path` | Folder where the HTML report is written. Defaults to the current folder. The file name is Diagnostics_<COMPUTER>_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.html. |
| `-PassThru` | switch |  | Also return the collected data as an object (useful for scripting). |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Get-SystemDiagnostics.ps1
```

Creates the HTML report in the current folder and prints a summary.

```powershell
.\Get-SystemDiagnostics.ps1 -OutputPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop" -PassThru
```

Writes the report to the Desktop and returns the data object.

## Notes

Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+. No admin rights needed. Related KB: KB-013 Computer Is Running Slow.
